articles.title: Real-world clinical outcomes under intravenous and subcutaneous esketamine protocols for treatment-resistant depression: a multicenter, retrospective study.
articles.abstract: Esketamine is a promising therapeutic option for treatment-resistant depression (TRD). Intravenous (IV) administration is the most extensively studied parenteral route. However, subcutaneous (SC) administration may offer simpler, more scalable delivery. Multicenter real-world evidence comparing IV and SC routes of administration remains limited. To report clinical outcomes and tolerability of parenteral esketamine protocols for TRD at three Brazilian advanced-care centers. This multicenter retrospective chart review study (2023-2025) included 72 outpatients aged 18-65 years who received esketamine 2 to 3 times weekly via IV (n = 26; 6 sessions) or SC (n = 46; 12 sessions) administration. Data were analyzed in RStudio 2026.01.0 Build 392 using R 4.5.2. The primary outcome was categorical response on the Beck Depression Inventory-II (BDI-II) at the shared 6-session milestone and at each protocol-specific endpoint. Secondary outcomes included continuous changes in BDI-II and Beck Anxiety Inventory (BAI) scores in the full sample, tolerability and documented adverse events, and exploratory factor analysis of baseline symptom dimensions. After six sessions, BDI-II response distribution favored the IV protocol, although the between-group difference was not statistically significant (Pearson's chi-square = 5.661; p = 0.059; odds ratio, 3.06; 95% CI, 1.22-8.00). At the protocol-specific endpoints, categorical BDI-II response did not differ significantly between groups (Pearson's chi-square = 1.227; p = 0.541; odds ratio, 1.44; 95% CI, 0.57-3.73). No serious adverse events or adverse-event-related discontinuations were reported; dissociation was more frequent with IV than with SC treatment (53.8% vs. 13.0%; p = 0.001), whereas nausea and mild transient blood pressure increases did not differ significantly. BDI-II factor analysis identified cognitive-affective and somatic-neurovegetative dimensions. The IV protocol showed a more favorable BDI-II response distribution at the shared 6-session milestone, whereas SC esketamine achieved statistically comparable categorical outcomes at its 12-session protocol-specific endpoint. Route selection should consider speed of response, tolerability, dosing, operational complexity, and access. SC esketamine may be a feasible option where simplicity, tolerability, and access are priorities. Results should be interpreted with caution because of the retrospective, observational study design.

articles.title: Oral Esketamine Maintenance Treatment for Treatment-Resistant Depression: Clinical Outcomes During an Off-Label Treatment Program.
articles.abstract: Ketamine and esketamine maintenance treatment show promise in maintaining initial antidepressant effects, yet further research is needed to optimize long-term outcomes. This observational study aimed to assess long-term depression symptom severity, safety, and tolerability in a cohort of patients receiving at-home oral esketamine maintenance treatment. Between June 2017 and March 2024, 221 patients with severe treatment-resistant unipolar depression were enrolled directly or trial-transferred into an off-label induction treatment program. After 6 weeks of individually titrated oral esketamine (twice a week, max 3.0 mg/kg) administered in the clinic, 93 patients continued to maintenance treatment at home (max 3.0 mg/kg twice a week). articles.title: MDMA-Assisted Therapy for Veterans with Comorbid Posttraumatic Stress Disorder and Alcohol Use Disorder: Clinical Outcomes from the First Open-Label Pilot Trial.
articles.abstract: Co-occurring posttraumatic stress disorder and alcohol use disorder (PTSD-AUD) are highly prevalent among U.S. Veterans and associated with greater symptom severity, functional impairment, and poorer outcomes than either disorder alone. Existing treatments demonstrate modest effectiveness, with persistent challenges in engagement, retention, and sustained improvement. To evaluate the feasibility, safety, tolerability, and preliminary clinical outcomes of investigational 3,4-methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA)-assisted therapy for Veterans with comorbid PTSD-AUD. We conducted the first open-label trial of MDMA-assisted therapy in Veterans (N = 10) with PTSD-AUD. The intervention included 11 therapy sessions (three preparatory, two MDMA assisted therapy sessions, and six integration), followed by a 4-week follow-up. Primary outcomes were PTSD symptom severity and alcohol consumption, measured by the Clinician-Administered PTSD Scale for DSM-5 (CAPS-5) and Timeline Follow-Back (TLFB). Secondary outcomes assessed safety and tolerability. Exploratory outcomes included alcohol craving and substance misuse. Recruitment and retention were strong with 90% of enrolled participants completing treatment. MDMA-assisted therapy was associated with significant reductions in PTSD symptoms (p = 0.006, d = 1.241). Descriptive reductions were observed in alcohol consumption, including a 31% reduction in drinks per drinking day and a 54% reduction in heavy drinking days, although these changes did not reach clinical significance. No serious adverse events were reported. Treatment-emergent adverse events were non-serious and consistent with expected acute MDMA effects under protocol monitoring. Substance-use measures did not indicate systematic increases in alcohol or other substance use; one participant reported an isolated recurrence of cocaine use. Findings support the safety, feasibility, and tolerability of MDMA-assisted therapy and provide preliminary descriptive evidence of improvement in PTSD symptoms and alcohol-related outcomes. Larger randomized controlled trials are needed to evaluate efficacy, durability, and benefit-risk profile in this population.

articles.title: Effects of psilocybin with psychological support on anhedonia in treatment-resistant depression: A randomized controlled pilot trial.
articles.abstract: Anhedonia is a core feature of major depressive disorder (MDD) that is frequently resistant to available treatments. Psilocybin's specific efficacy for anhedonia remains unclear. To evaluate psilocybin's efficacy for anhedonia in treatment-resistant MDD. In this randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 20 participants with treatment-resistant MDD received psilocybin (25 mg or 1 mg) with psychological support. The primary outcome was change in the Dimensional Anhedonia Rating Scale (DARS) score at week 1; DARS change at week 8 was a secondary outcome. The Snaith-Hamilton Pleasure Scale (SHAPS) and Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS) were used as additional secondary outcome measures for anhedonia and overall depression severity, respectively. The primary outcome was not statistically significant: between-group difference in DARS change at week 1 was 11.2 (95% confidence interval [CI], -1.0 to 23.3; p = 0.073). At week 8, the secondary DARS outcome indicated greater improvement in anhedonia with 25 mg (difference, 14.7; 95% CI, 2.5 to 26.8; p = 0.018). SHAPS improvement favored 25 mg at week 1 (difference, -3.2; 95% CI, -6.1 to -0.3; p = 0.029), but not week 8 (-2.1; 95% CI, -4.9 to 0.9; p = 0.168). MADRS improvement favored 25 mg at weeks 1 (-11.9; 95% CI, -19.2 to -4.5; p = 0.002) and 8 (-11.6; 95% CI, -19.0 to -4.2; p = 0.002). Psilocybin 25 mg did not significantly improve anhedonia at the primary week 1 endpoint. However, improvements on secondary measures suggest potential benefits for anhedonia and depression severity that warrant confirmation in larger trials. ClinicalTrials.govNCT06230757.

articles.title: Rapid antidepressant effects of ketamine combined with selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors: Mechanisms and outlook.
articles.abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is a prevalent and disabling psychiatric illness. Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs), while the cornerstone of first-line pharmacotherapy, are limited by delayed therapeutic onset and high rates of nonresponse or partial response. Our previous work demonstrated that a single subanesthetic dose of ketamine or its enantiomers can accelerate SSRI response and enhance efficacy in patients with residual fluctuations after initial improvement. We hypothesize that this combination is synergistic rather than merely additive, although the precise mechanisms remain to be fully characterized. Synthesizing these observations with a comprehensive literature review, we propose the GLIMPSE model (Glu-GABA Long-circuit Integrative Metaplasticity for Psychopathology and Synaptic Efficacy), an integrative framework positing that the dorsal raphe-prefrontal cortex 5-HT-glutamate/GABA circuit functions as an upstream driver, whereas metaplasticity and synaptic priming serve as the key downstream convergence points for ketamine-SSRI synergy. Building on this framework, we further outline a practical safety-monitoring protocol for serotonin syndrome associated with this combination, alongside a future-oriented research agenda grounded in the GLIMPSE model to guide subsequent mechanistic and clinical investigations.

articles.title: Shared pain, shared decisions: Effects of empathic engagement on social conformity and decision processes, with physiological and visual-attentional associations.
articles.abstract: Empathy enables individuals to attune to others' experiences through shared affective, sensorimotor, and neural representations. Although central to emotional understanding, empathic engagement may extend beyond affective resonance to shape higher-level cognitive processes. In particular, empathic engagement may promote social alignment, biasing individuals to adjust their decisions toward others'. However, it remains unknown whether experimentally induced empathic-engagement instructions influence conformity in decision-making and whether conformity under this condition is associated with physiological responses, visual attention, and individual differences in socio-emotional traits. Here, 73 participants completed an empathy-for-pain task and performed a modified random-dot task in which they interacted with empathy targets. Physiological signals were recorded during the empathy manipulation, while eye movements were tracked throughout the task. Using switching rate as a measure of conformity, we found that feedback from empathy targets increased conformity. Computational drift-diffusion modeling showed that the empathic engagement condition was associated with stronger decision bias toward targets and altered drift rate. Depending on the context, visual attention to the eyes and mouth was associated with greater conformity. Larger increases in phasic skin conductance from the detached-observation to empathic engagement condition were associated with greater decision conservatism and reduced decision bias. Finally, alexithymia and autistic traits moderated the relationship between empathy and conformity separately, but not jointly. These findings show that the effects of empathic engagement instructions may extend beyond affective resonance to influence subsequent decision-making. More broadly, they suggest that social alignment may be related to socio-emotional traits, with exploratory associations involving physiological arousal and visual attention.

articles.title: Predictive value of EEG/ECG biomarkers for treatment response in depression.
articles.abstract: Major depressive episodes frequently show limited response to first-line treatments, motivating the search for objective biomarkers. EEG/ECG-based support tools aggregating electrophysiological predictors may guide treatment selection. We examined whether antidepressant treatments concordant with an EEG/ECG-biomarker report were associated with higher response rates. We retrospectively analyzed adults with ICD-10 depressive disorder or bipolar depression treated with electroconvulsive therapy (ECT), repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS), (es)ketamine, or selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) between 2022 and 2024. Resting-state EEG with simultaneous ECG generated individualized biomarker reports with modality-specific response likelihoods. Treatment chosen by clinical teams was classified as concordant or non-concordant; response was derived from routinely collected clinical scales. Among 153 patients (ECT n = 53, rTMS n = 48, (es)ketamine n = 36, SSRIs n = 16), response rates were higher for concordant vs non-concordant treatments: ECT 70% vs 50%, rTMS 30% vs 13%, (es)ketamine 31% vs 10%, and SSRIs 100% vs 11%. Overall, 46% (42/92) of concordant vs. 26% (14/54) of non-concordant patients responded (absolute difference + 20 percentage points; relative increase ≈77%; number needed to treat ≈5). Concordance with EEG/ECG biomarkers correlated with higher treatment response, warranting confirmation in prospective trials. EEG/ECG-based decision support may enhance antidepressant treatment response in everyday clinical practice.

articles.title: The Fireside Database: Large-scale evidence from 25,419 psychedelic support interactions.
articles.abstract: Most psychedelic experiences occur outside clinical settings, yet as policy frameworks rapidly expand to accommodate nonclinical use, no systematic data exist on who seeks psychedelic support, under what circumstances, or what makes that support effective. We present the Fireside Database, a US-based dataset comprising 25,419 peer support interactions conducted by 220 trained volunteers at Fireside Project's Psychedelic Support Line between April 2021 and February 2026. The released resource integrates structured interaction logs with volunteer-coded metadata and 2777 caller satisfaction surveys across five outcome dimensions. Psilocybin was the most commonly reported substance (59.9% of coded interactions), while cannabis produced the highest distress rate (47.2%). The nested data structure-with 50 supporters each completing ≥10 surveyed interactions-supports multilevel modeling of individual supporter effects on caller outcomes. This resource enables research in psychedelic epidemiology, evidence-based training design, and the investigation of what makes psychedelic psychological support effective.

articles.title: Efficacy, safety, and tolerability of lysergic acid diethylamide for the treatment of depressive symptoms: A meta-analysis and systematic review.
articles.abstract: Since the Food and Drug Administration designated lysergic acid diethylamide (LSD) as a "breakthrough" treatment for generalized anxiety disorder, accumulating randomized clinical trials (RCTs) evaluating LSD's anxiolytic effects have also reported improved depression symptoms. Evaluating the safety and efficacy of LSD in treating depression symptoms is warranted. MEDLINE/PubMED, Embase, and PsychINFO were searched from inception to December 9, 2025. RCTs evaluating efficacy of LSD on depression symptoms in adults with mental disorders were included. Cochrane Risk of Bias Tool 2.0 and χ Of 465 screened studies, 5 RCTs met selection criteria ( Our findings suggest that LSD, with and without psychological support, reduces depression scores in clinical populations. This review is limited by small sample size. Future well-designed RCTs are needed to establish the efficacy and safety of LSD in managing depression.

articles.title: Evolutionary neuropharmacology of serotonergic psychedelics: a cross-species perspective on mechanisms, consciousness, and therapeutic potential.
articles.abstract: Serotonergic psychedelics have revitalized psychiatric research by producing rapid and potentially sustained clinical benefits in selected neuropsychiatric conditions. However, the mechanisms linking receptor activation to neural plasticity, altered conscious experience, and clinical improvement remain incompletely understood, while the evolutionary origins of psychedelic signaling and the translational value of animal models continue to be actively debated. In this review, we integrate evolutionary biology, molecular pharmacology, comparative neuroscience, and computational psychiatry into a unified framework for understanding psychedelic action across biological scales. Building upon predictive processing and the Relaxed Beliefs Under Psychedelics (REBUS) framework, we discuss how serotonergic psychedelics transiently reshape hierarchical inference, providing computational principles that can be experimentally investigated across species despite profound differences in neural architecture and subjective experience. Comparative analyses from invertebrates to non-human primates further suggest that conserved receptor pharmacology coexists with species-specific circuit organization, highlighting that animal models should be interpreted as complementary platforms for investigating molecular, cellular, and computational mechanisms rather than direct proxies for human hallucinatory experiences. We further discuss preclinical and emerging translational evidence suggesting that biased receptor signaling and non-hallucinogenic psychoplastogens may partially dissociate plasticity-related therapeutic actions from hallucinogenic effects, providing new opportunities for mechanism-based drug development. By integrating evolutionary biology with molecular psychiatry, this review provides a mechanistic framework linking receptor pharmacology, neural plasticity, circuit computation, and therapeutic outcomes, thereby offering new conceptual and experimental strategies for developing next-generation psychedelic therapeutics.

articles.title: Cross-species mapping of acute psychedelic-responsive genes links HTR2A cortical expression, cell-type enrichment, and human cortical expression modules.
articles.abstract: Psychedelic drugs exert rapid and profound effects on human consciousness [1-7] and are increasingly being investigated for their therapeutic potential [8-14]. Yet the transcriptional programs through which they may reshape brain function and structure remain incompletely understood, in part because the available evidence is heterogeneous and largely preclinical [15, 16]. In a structured scoping review of transcriptomic studies in animal models and neural cell cultures, we identified genes reported in the source literature to change within 3 h of classical psychedelic administration and intersected them with the Allen Human Brain Atlas to define an acute expression set. This retained set showed cortex-centered enrichment, a marker-based deep-layer projection-neuron component, and ontology enrichment for neuron projection and related synaptic terms. A smaller subset overlapped with human accelerated region-associated genes and showed greater-than-random spatial alignment with a human cortical-expansion map. The retained cortical-expression maps showed serotonergic spatial alignment in the human cortex, most prominently with HTR2A expression. Clustering identified three cortical spatial-expression modules, including an association/limbic-weighted module enriched for plasticity and synaptic-organization terms. Together, these findings provide a human cortical framework linking acute psychedelic-responsive transcription to cortical cell-type enrichment, HTR2A spatial expression, cortical spatial-expression modules, and cortical-expansion, while leaving receptor-specific, causal, translational, and cell-type-resolved mechanisms for future work.

articles.title: Locus coeruleus noradrenergic neurons have diverse activity patterns across species and biological context.
articles.abstract: The locus coeruleus (LC) brainstem cell group is evolutionarily conserved across vertebrates and influences both mind (cognition) and body (cardiorespiratory, metabolic, and immune functions) via two-putatively distinct-spontaneous activity patterns. Yet, the degree to which spontaneous LC firing rates and patterns are homogeneous across species has never been assessed due to inherently limited sample sizes. To remedy this, we pooled cross-species data from 20 laboratories to show that firing rates differ across species and are modulated by sex, age, and type of in vitro or in vivo preparation. Contrary to the prevailing dual-mode firing pattern schema, we observed patterns spread across a low-dimensional manifold, with subregions enriched for specific biological factors and neurodegenerative disease models. Our findings show considerable diversity in an ancestral vertebrate neuromodulatory system.

articles.title: Participant experiences and recommendations for psychedelic clinical trials and future treatment delivery: a qualitative study with experts by experience from the Psychedelic Participant Advocacy Network.
articles.abstract: While psychedelic treatments for difficult-to-treat mental health conditions are advancing, participant perspectives remain under-explored. This study examined former participants' experiences across recruitment, preparation, dosing, integration and study ending, and generated recommendations for future trials and treatment delivery. This qualitative descriptive study, informed by reflexive thematic analysis, included four Psychedelic Participant Advocacy Network (PsyPAN) members who were former psychedelic-trial participants. They completed three remote focus groups on recruitment and screening, preparation and dosing, and post-dose integration and the post-study period. Three had joined treatment-resistant depression studies involving psilocybin or N,N-dimethyltryptamine; one had joined a psilocybin study for an eating disorder. A one-day workshop reviewed the analysis and developed recommendations, refined with wider PsyPAN input. Five themes were developed. First, participants entered trials seeking potentially effective treatment but encountered procedures shaped by eligibility criteria, equipoise, randomization, blinding, standardization, fixed schedules and endpoint-driven evidence generation. Second, participants' accounts extended "set and setting" to the clinical-trial context by showing how research-specific conditions, including treatment-allocation uncertainty, communication, staff conduct, time-limited support, study ending and the wider support matrix, shaped experience and could mitigate tensions between treatment-seeking and research requirements. Third, facilitators mediated between protocol requirements and participants' embodied, relational and psychological needs, particularly during dosing. Fourth, dosing was experienced as the beginning of an ongoing process of meaning-making, change and integration. Fifth, experiences after study ending varied; some participants described loss, grief or frustration, while all reported that further structured support would have been beneficial. They highlighted limited access to psychedelically informed care and advocated independent, trial-specific peer support. Recommendations emphasized clear communication, expectation management, distinction between research and treatment frames, reduced avoidable burden, staff continuity, participant agency, boundaries around touch and movement, involvement of support networks, and planning for integration and study ending. Relational, contextual and systemic factors shaped participants' experiences across recruitment, preparation, dosing, integration and study ending. Participant-informed practices should be considered when designing and delivering psychedelic studies, while recognizing scientific, regulatory and resource constraints. Structured post-study peer support may address continuing support needs after trial completion.

articles.title: Association between peripheral hsa-miR-4456 expression and plasma oxytocin in men with hypersexual disorder and healthy controls: a secondary cross-sectional analysis.
articles.abstract: MicroRNAs are candidate regulators and biomarkers of molecular processes relevant to behavior, but their relationships with neuroendocrine signaling in humans remain poorly characterized. Earlier studies in overlapping cohorts identified hypermethylation-associated downregulation of peripheral blood-derived hsa-miR-4456 in men with hypersexual disorder and implicated oxytocin-related pathways through  We performed a secondary cross-sectional analysis of baseline, pretreatment measurements from clinically characterized men with hypersexual disorder and healthy male controls. miR-4456 was measured by RT-qPCR in EDTA blood-derived material and plasma oxytocin by radioimmunoassay. The submitted pooled robust regression included 74 paired measurements; revised group-adjusted and interaction models included 73 complete cases (51 hypersexual disorder and 22 controls). miR-4456, but not oxytocin, was rank-based inverse-normal transformed using Blom's method. In the submitted pooled model, higher miR-4456 was associated with lower plasma oxytocin (β = -4.039 pmol/L, 95% CI -6.149 to -1.930;  To our knowledge, this is the first human study to directly examine paired peripheral miR-4456 and plasma oxytocin measurements. Although diagnostic-group differences explained part of the pooled association, the paired observation connects previously separate epigenetic, expression, pathway-prediction, and neuroendocrine findings and identifies a focused hypothesis for independent replication. The cross-sectional peripheral measurements do not establish directionality, causation, or central nervous system regulation. Experimental studies are needed to determine whether miR-4456 has any functional influence on oxytocin-related biology.

articles.title: Gut consciousness: a perspective on visceral phenomenal awareness.
articles.abstract: The proposition that the enteric nervous system sustains a form of consciousness is seldom entertained in mainstream neuroscience, yet it follows from a disciplined reading of contemporary theories of mind. We argue that the 400-600 million neurons embedded in the mammalian gastrointestinal wall, taken together with the vast interoceptive surface they supervise, the enteroendocrine-immune interface, and the microbial community they co-regulate, constitute a substrate that satisfies, on several of the leading theories of consciousness, the criteria those theories use to attribute experience elsewhere. We synthesize evidence on enteric autonomy, chemo- and mechanosensory resolution, vagal and humoral signalling, self/non-self-discrimination at the epithelial-immune boundary, comparative data from invertebrates whose nervous systems are dominated by gut-like plexuses, and convergent clinical signatures (irritable bowel syndrome, food intolerances, psychedelic nausea, glucagon-like peptide-1 signalling) that are difficult to accommodate under a purely sensorimotor account. Throughout we distinguish two claims that are easily conflated: that the gut makes a large and underappreciated contribution to the single consciousness of the whole animal, and that enteric processing constitutes a second, much simpler locus of experience of its own. Most of the available evidence bears on the first, and we set out five lines of investigation that would discriminate between them. We conclude that gut consciousness is a testable hypothesis, likely corresponding to an 'animal' mode of consciousness dominated by interoceptive feel, drive and affect, and we propose empirical directions for its further investigation.

articles.title: Update on Sedation for Upper Gastrointestinal Endoscopy in Japan: Current Evidence on Remimazolam.
articles.abstract: Sedation is an essential component of upper gastrointestinal endoscopy because it reduces patient discomfort and anxiety while improving patient acceptance and procedural quality. In Japan, benzodiazepines such as midazolam and opioid analgesics have long been widely used in routine clinical practice; however, many of these agents historically lacked formal insurance approval for sedation during gastrointestinal endoscopy. Propofol is also a useful sedative because of its rapid onset and recovery, but its use in Japan has been limited because of concerns regarding respiratory and cardiovascular depression and the need for management by anesthesia-trained personnel. Against this background, the approval of remimazolam for sedation during gastrointestinal endoscopy in June 2025 represented a major turning point in Japanese endoscopic sedation practice. Remimazolam is an ultra-short-acting benzodiazepine rapidly metabolized by carboxylesterases and reversible with flumazenil. Japanese phase III trials demonstrated high sedation success rates and rapid recovery during upper gastrointestinal endoscopy, including in elderly patients. Compared with midazolam, remimazolam shortened awakening and ambulation times, whereas compared with propofol, it may cause fewer respiratory and cardiovascular adverse events. This review summarizes the current status of upper gastrointestinal endoscopic sedation in Japan, focusing on the clinical evidence and positioning of the newly approved ultra-short-acting benzodiazepine, remimazolam.

articles.title: Tissue engineering polymeric formulations enable lymphangiogenesis for myocardial repair.
articles.abstract:
Purpose

Emerging evidence emphasizes the pivotal contribution of cardiac lymphatic activation following ischemic heart injury, with induced lymphangiogenesis driving edema resolution and inflammatory cell clearance. The aim of this study was to identify a bioactive small molecule with pro-lymphangiogenic activity and to develop a tissue engineering polymeric formulation for sustained local delivery in myocardial repair.

Methods

Through a high-throughput screen, we identified the bioactive molecule β-(3,4-dihydroxyphenyl) lactic acid (3,4-DHPLA) as a potent stimulator of lymphatic endothelial cells (LECs). To leverage this finding, we engineered a tissue engineering polymeric formulation (TEPF) to promote lymphangiogenesis during myocardial repair. The TEPF was fabricated via an integrated strategy combining 3D printing and near-field electrospinning to incorporate 3,4-DHPLA into a biodegradable polyurethane scaffold. The resulting structure mimics the microstructure of the cardiac extracellular matrix while supporting the microenvironment-responsive release of 3,4-DHPLA.

Results

We evaluated the therapeutic efficacy of TEPF in rat and porcine ischemia/reperfusion injury models, which markedly improved cardiac function and significantly attenuated adverse ventricular remodeling. Single-cell RNA sequencing and in vitro data further revealed the dual mechanisms of TEPF, not only promoting lymphangiogenesis but also orchestrating a pro-regenerative niche via expansion of Tregs, M2 macrophages, and pro-regenerative fibroblasts (COL12A1+, COL11A1+, NRG1+).

Conclusions

Thus, the tissue engineering polymeric formulations may enable sustained drug release during myocardial tissue repair, thereby alleviating the pain of injection administration for patients with cardiovascular diseases and potentially facilitating patient-friendly use of other functional molecules-based therapeutic tissue engineering formulations through durable delivery.

articles.title: Glis1 regulates metabolic programming by promoting H3K18 lactylation to alleviate neuronal senescence following spinal cord injury.
articles.abstract: Neuronal senescence is a significant factor impeding spinal cord injury (SCI) repair. Research indicates that Glis1, a Kruppel-like zinc finger transcription factor, is pivotal in reprogramming senescent cells and enhancing genomic stability via lactylation. Histone lactylation, an epigenetic modification using lactate as a substrate, becomes prominent post-SCI due to increased neuronal lactate levels. However, the mechanisms linking neuronal senescence and histone lactylation following SCI remain poorly understood. This study elucidates the roles of Glis1, H3K18 lactylation, and neuronal senescence through comprehensive in vivo and in vitro investigations. The findings reveal a post-SCI rise in neuronal lactate levels, accompanied by cellular senescence. Furthermore, upregulation of Glis1 attenuates senescence and promotes histone lactylation. The downstream target secretogranin II (SCG2), identified via ChIP-seq and RNA-seq, was found to exert negative feedback on glycolytic metabolism and lactylation, thereby suppressing neuronal senescence. These results unveil a novel regulatory mechanism of Glis1 in neuronal senescence following SCI through the p300/H3K18la/SCG2 axis, offering a new therapeutic target for spinal cord repair.

articles.title: A bioactivity-enhanced thermosensitive amnion-derived hydrogel with sustained IGF-1 release: A multitargeted and efficient strategy for corneal injury repair.
articles.abstract: Corneal alkali burn (CAB) remains difficult to treat because rapid tear clearance limits topical drug exposure, while the injured cornea develops a complex microenvironment involving inflammation, neovascularization, fibrosis, epithelial barrier loss, and impaired nerve repair. Here, we developed a human amniotic membrane-derived thermosensitive hydrogel (hAMgel) and loaded it with insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) to create a bioactive sustained-release system (IGF1@hAMgel) for CAB repair. The hAMgel transformed from a flowable precursor into a semi-transparent film on the ocular surface within 1-2 min and IGF1@hAMgel released approximately 90% of loaded IGF-1 over 24 h, with corneal IGF-1 concentration peaking at 2 h post-dose (378.5 pg/mg protein) and remaining detectable over 24 h, supporting sustained topical exposure. In a rat CAB model, IGF1@hAMgel accelerated epithelial healing, reducing the fluorescein-stained area from 31.34 ± 2.83% in controls to 16.78 ± 2.87% at day 1. By day 14, IGF1@hAMgel reduced corneal opacity (0.67 ± 0.52 vs. 4.00 ± 0.00), resolved edema with central corneal thickness approaching baseline (187.7 ± 16.31 μm vs. 178.3 ± 5.89 μm), suppressed neovascularization (CD31-positive area 4.46 ± 1.69% vs. 24.33 ± 2.07%), and promoted corneal nerve regeneration. Proteomic analysis showed that hAMgel retained abundant extracellular matrix(ECM) components, including collagens, Lumican, and fibronectin, together with repair-related and immunomodulatory proteins. These findings identify IGF1@hAMgel as a sutureless, eye-drop-like bioactive ECM platform that integrates growth-factor delivery with amnion-derived reparative cues for multitargeted ocular surface repair.

articles.title: A self-crosslinkable, adhesive intestine-derived extracellular matrix hydrogel enhances organoid retention and restores intestinal barrier integrity.
articles.abstract: Disruption of the intestinal barrier impairs essential functions of the gastrointestinal tract and triggers severe inflammation. Accordingly, transplantation of intestinal organoids restores the integrity of the injured intestinal barrier by promoting regeneration. However, the dynamic mucosal microenvironment of the intestine hinders effective retention of transplanted organoids, thereby limiting their therapeutic efficacy. To address this challenge, this study introduces a pyrogallol (PG)-conjugated intestine-derived extracellular matrix (IEM) (IEM-PG) as a scaffold for effective organoid transplantation. The dual crosslinking of IEM-based fibrillogenesis and oxidative PG coupling enabled IEM-PG to form a robust hydrogel scaffold without crosslinking agents under physiological conditions. Moreover, the IEM-PG hydrogel exhibited enhanced mechanical properties, superior bio-adhesion, and greater resistance to enzymatic degradation than the pristine IEM. The IEM-PG hydrogel was also highly biocompatible and did not adversely affect the viability and development of colonic organoids. The solution-type IEM-PG was readily injected into colonic tissue, thus allowing IEM-PG to initially spread along the intestinal lining. Transplantation of colonic organoids using IEM-PG in a mouse colonic ulcer model demonstrated effective cell retention in the intestinal tract, thereby restoring the structural integrity and function of the intestinal barrier. The study further demonstrated that the patch-type IEM-PG hydrogel was effective for the transplantation of colonic assembloids and the treatment of colonic perforation. Overall, this study presents the IEM engineered with an adhesive motif as a self-crosslinking hydrogel platform for organoid/assembloid transplantation and intestinal tissue repair.

articles.title: Barcoded oligonucleotide system (BOLT) for targeted organ delivery.
articles.abstract: The therapeutic potential of oligonucleotides (oligos) is limited by insufficient delivery to extrahepatic tissues. In vitro assays often fail to accurately predict in vivo behavior, while testing each oligo candidate in animals remains inherently low throughput. Here, we conceive a barcoded oligonucleotide system (BOLT), a platform that enables high-throughput in vivo evaluations of small-molecule ligands and identifies tissue-specific oligo delivery. BOLT integrates rational design of oligo barcodes, modular conjugation chemistry, and next-generation sequencing (NGS)-based quantification, allowing simultaneous evaluation of many chemically diverse ligand-oligo conjugates within a single animal. Notably, this platform is applicable in both mice and nonhuman primates (NHPs). Using BOLT, we discovered ligands with tropism for tissues such as the brain, lung, and muscle. Collectively, these results indicate that the BOLT platform can accelerate the discovery of tissue-targeting ligands for broad oligo therapeutics.

articles.title: Ultrasound-activated piezoelectric muscle constructs for tissue-engineered regenerative peripheral nerve interfaces.
articles.abstract: Regenerative peripheral nerve interfaces (RPNIs) are emerging platforms capable to translate neural activity into controllable myoelectric signals. However, current clinical RPNIs rely on muscle autografts, limiting their scalability and extensive adoption. Here, we report a bioactive, ultrasound-responsive piezoelectric muscle biomaterial designed as a fully tissue-engineered alternative to autologous grafts. The construct consists of fibrinogen-based muscle tissues enriched with barium titanate nanoparticles (BTNPs, diameter∼60 nm) and supported by a biodegradable surgical membrane that promotes the formation of aligned, multinucleated myotubes. The incorporation of BTNPs imparts intrinsic piezoelectric activity to the construct, and the nanoparticles are taken up by developing myotubes, enabling remote mechanoelectrical tissue stimulation under low-intensity pulsed ultrasound (LIPUS). In vivo, piezoelectric constructs implanted around the rat peroneal nerve for two months undergo LIPUS-driven activation of internalized BTNPs, which enhances muscle maturation, and electromechanical responsiveness, yielding myoelectrical signals up to 3.2 mV upon nerve activation. Histological analyses confirm improved structural organization, increased desmin expression, and evidence of neovascularization and axonal regeneration within the engineered interface. These findings suggest that the piezoelectric constructs form stable, functional biointerfaces with peripheral nerves, and that LIPUS-driven activation of embedded BTNPs provides a non-invasive strategy to potentiate muscle development and signal transduction. This study positions LIPUS-responsive, engineered piezoelectric muscle constructs as a donor-free, bioactive platform alternative to traditional autografts for next-generation human-machine interfaces and regenerative bioelectronics.

articles.title: <b>Chicoric acid regulates IL-1β to improve the inflammatory response in mice undergoing myomectomy under propofol anesthesia</b>.
articles.abstract:
Background

Surgical excision of uterine fibroids triggers acute inflammation, impacting postoperative recovery. Propofol anesthesia may modulate this response. Chicoric acid possesses anti-inflammatory properties, but its perioperative utility remains unexplored.

Objectives

To investigate whether preoperative chicoric acid enhances the anti-inflammatory effect of propofol in a mouse model of myomectomy and to explore the involvement of the p38 MAPK/NF-κB/IL-1β axis.

Methods

A human uterine fibroid xenograft mouse model was established using CB-17 SCID mice. Mice underwent simulated myomectomy under propofol or ketamine anesthesia, with or without preoperative chicoric acid (50 mg/kg, 7 days). Controls included sham and model groups. The p38 MAPK/NF-κB agonist LPS and the IL-1β blocker Rilonacept were used to probe mechanisms. Inflammatory cytokines (MSD), pathway protein expression (Western blot), and uterine histopathology (H&E) were assessed 12h post-surgery.

Results

Propofol anesthesia significantly inhibited surgery-induced p38 MAPK/NF-κB activation and reduced levels of inflammatory cytokines compared with the model group. Preoperative cholic acid further suppressed this pathway and enhanced the anti-inflammatory effect beyond that of propofol alone. LPS reversed chicoric acid's effects, confirming the involvement of the pathway. Unexpectedly, Rilonacept did not enhance but rather reversed the anti-inflammatory effect of chicoric acid, suggesting complex, compensatory interactions within a cytokine network.

Conclusion

Preoperative chicoric acid augments propofol's anti-inflammatory effect during myomectomy by inhibiting the p38 MAPK/NF-κB pathway. However, the paradoxical effect of IL-1β blockade reveals unforeseen complexity in the perioperative cytokine network, warranting further investigation into the multitarget effects of chicoric acid and potential network-compensation mechanisms.

articles.title: Human-Derived Motor Neuron Progenitor Cell Implantation Rescues Motor Endplates Following Peripheral Nerve Injury.
articles.abstract:
Purpose

Degradation of motor endplates (MEPs) following peripheral nerve injury (PNI) is a major determinant of functional recovery, as prolonged denervation renders target muscles progressively unreceptive to reinnervation. While prior studies have demonstrated that stem cell-based therapies may provide neurotrophic support following PNI, their potential effects on MEP preservation have not been well studied. We hypothesized that transplantation of human-induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC)-derived motor neuron progenitors (MNPs) into chronically denervated muscle would be associated with preservation of MEP architecture.

Methods

With Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee approval, chronic denervation injuries were created in mice via sciatic nerve transection. After 4 months of denervation, when MEPs have consistently degraded in this animal model, the denervated tibialis anterior (TA) was injected with low-dose MNPs (10,000 cells), high-dose MNPs (500,000 cells), or phosphate-buffered saline (negative control). Using a previously established method, hiPSCs were differentiated into functional MNPs prior to injection. At selected time points post-injection, the TA was harvested and immunostained to confirm MNP viability and detect the presence of MEPs.

Results

Transplanted MNPs remained viable within host muscle at both evaluated time points. No identifiable MEPs were detected in phosphate-buffered saline-treated chronically denervated muscle. In contrast, MNP-treated muscles demonstrated the presence of MEP-like structures following prolonged denervation. Qualitative differences in MEP density and morphologic complexity were observed between treatment groups, with greater preservation seen in the higher-dose cohort. Contralateral uninjured muscles demonstrated intact native MEP architecture.

Conclusions

Intramuscular transplantation of hiPSC-derived MNPs into chronically denervated muscle was associated with preservation of MEP morphology in this preclinical proof-of-concept model. These preliminary findings suggest that cellular therapies may represent a potential adjunctive strategy to preserve end-organ receptivity following delayed peripheral nerve injury.

Type of study/level of evidence

Preclinical controlled animal study, Level V.

articles.title: From data to wisdom: A new era of scientific inquiry.
articles.abstract: Rapid advances in high-throughput technologies and computational tools have ushered in a transformative era for scientific discovery. However, the acceleration of data generation has outpaced our conceptual frameworks for interpreting it. By examining current challenges in drug discovery, phenotypic screening, and model transferability, I argue that the future of scientific integrity depends on our ability to balance technical proficiency with the classical principles of hypothesis negation. Because the scientists who interpret data are themselves prone to bias and error, these safeguards must apply to human judgment as rigorously as to computational tools. I also confront a central tension: the mechanistic understanding I advocate may not scale to systems of cellular complexity. Finally, I propose a collaborative training approach that sustains both experimental excellence and theoretical depth. Each challenge maps onto the Data-Information-Knowledge-Wisdom (DIKW) hierarchy: failures at the D→I transition (underdetermined models), at I→K (undefined null hypotheses and black-box modeling), at K→W (non-transferable animal models and cross-domain blindness), or in the collapse of the entire chain when paradigm inertia forecloses the revision that wisdom demands.
